## The two demonstrations, with their cells

**1. The `O` cell that a barrier does not rescue.**
Sulfuric acid (`8`) against calcium hypochlorite
(`5.1`). The 177.848(d) cell for row "Corrosive liquids"
against column "5.1" is **`O`**, which on its face means the two may
travel together once separated. 177.848(e)(3) then removes that option outright:
Class 8 liquids may not be loaded above or adjacent to Class 5 materials
regardless of separation. An agent reasoning from the matrix alone clears this
load.

**2. The material with no UN number.**
Ammonium chlorate is `Forbidden` and has no identification number.
49 CFR 173.21(a) forbids offering for transportation:

> Materials that are designated "Forbidden" in Column 3 of the § 172.101 table. (b) Forbidden explosives as defined in § 1

and 172.101(d)(1):

> A material for which the entry in this column is "Forbidden" may not be offered for transportation or transported.

Any index keyed on a UN number returns nothing for all 256 of these.
